mechanism_claims.claim_text: Arenicin-3, tachyplesin-1, polyphemusin-1, gomesin, and protegrin-1 showed direct E. coli ATCC 25922 inner membrane permeabilization in the SYTOX Green flow-cytometry assay at lethal concentrations.
direct_assay_types: SYTOX Green inner membrane permeability flow cytometry

source_locator.locator: supp:id6b00045_si_001.pdf:Figure S3 and Inner membrane permeability method

mechanism_claims.limitations: Figure S3 exact per-peptide dose-response values were not text-tabulated; claim is qualitative/direct for permeability and keeps lethal-concentration range as reported in text.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Thanatin did not permeabilize E. coli cells at lethal concentrations in the same SYTOX Green assay, so this paper does not support assigning thanatin killing to cytoplasmic membrane permeabilization.
direct_assay_types: SYTOX Green inner membrane permeability flow cytometry
mechanism_claims.limitations: The paper cites prior literature for thanatin agglutination; that literature-derived mechanism is not promoted to a direct mechanism of this paper.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The paper correlates amphipathicity, hydrophobicity, antimicrobial potency, and toxicity across beta-hairpin peptides, but those correlations are physicochemical context rather than standalone direct mechanism assays.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Correlation figures are not overclaimed as direct membrane-disruption proof.
